title: World Models: Definition, Clarification, Distinction, and Boundaries（世界模型：定义、澄清、区别与边界）
description: Sixth paper of the human-referential fitting theory program. Between 2024 and 2026, "world model" expanded from a reinforcement-learning textbook term into a high-frequency word shared by industry and the academy, without consensus on what it fundamentally is. This paper extends the program's conceptual toolkit to the term with four contributions. (1) Definition: the world model is a functional, not an entity, concept—a system has one relative to an environment and an action space iff it possesses an action-conditioned, interventional, repeatedly callable prediction capability; implementation splits into written-in, learned, and learn-then-formalize families. (2) Clarification: the confusion is not semantic vagueness but positional polymorphism—one functional concept located at four positions (agent's component, evaluator's benchmark, planner's state representation, trainer's simulated environment), with four forms of invocation; definitional disputes reduce to disputes over positions. (3) Analysis: three propositions—perspective is a property of position; the probability share is a function of the observation position, with calibration as the test standard; environment members divide by the origin of their tasks, and where physics runs out is where agents begin—plus a limit on recursive self-improvement: sustainable self-improvement must retain real-data admixture, and calibration cannot self-certify. (4) Distinctions: from intelligence (policy versus model; acting and predicting do not imply each other) and from AGI (criterial mismatch; component progress is non-transferable), with a structural analysis of the terminal "intelligent world model" in four routes, four requirements, and three boundaries. Eight falsifiability clauses and an admission protocol for new cases close the paper.
notes: Manuscript in English and Chinese editions (paper.pdf / paper_zh.pdf). Part of the human-referential fitting theory program; theory paper: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23391808.
